blocks.title: Socializing
blocks.goal: Help each child join play and make a choice without pressure to speak publicly.
blocks.prepare: Place the five choice cards at a low table near the arrival area; leave other familiar play materials accessible.
steps: Greet the child by name. Offer two concrete play options already available.
If the child wants help joining peers, model: ‘May I build with you?’ Give peers time to respond.
Acknowledge the choice: ‘You chose blocks today.’ A child may point or begin playing instead of answering.
Near 10:00, give a two-minute warning, then guide cleanup and handwashing.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘You can choose what you would like to try. We do not all have to choose the same thing.’
blocks.child_action: Choose, point, speak, or join an activity; practice an invitation or turn-taking when appropriate.
blocks.look_for: Can the child enter play with or without a prompt? Note support needed, not a pass/fail grade.
blocks.assistant: Welcome new arrivals while the lead teacher supports a child who needs help joining play.
blocks.materials: Five printed choice cards; existing blocks, books, paper, and outdoor movement space.

blocks.title: P.E.
blocks.goal: Follow a simple movement sequence and notice personal space.
blocks.prepare: Choose a clear outdoor area with room to extend arms; no equipment is required.
steps: Ask children to make ‘airplane arms’ and check that they are not touching a neighbor.
Model four slow movements: march eight steps; reach high four times; bend knees four times; balance on each foot for a short count.
Repeat the sequence once. Offer wall or adult support for balancing.
Finish with two slow breaths and walk to the next outdoor activity.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘Find your own space. Move in a way that feels comfortable for your body.’
blocks.child_action: Follow or adapt the four movements.
blocks.look_for: Notices space around others and can switch movements with a cue.
blocks.assistant: Model an accessible version beside children who need it; keep a clear path.
blocks.materials: Open outdoor space; optional stable support for balance.

blocks.title: Large Circle
blocks.goal: Express one preference and hear that classmates may choose differently.
blocks.prepare: Cut out and arrange the five printable choice cards in view; have the teacher display story ready for later.
steps: Start with a brief welcome. Show READ, BUILD, DRAW, MOVE, and SOMETHING ELSE one at a time.
Model one genuine choice: ‘I like to draw. I also like to try building.’ Do not imply that one activity is best.
Invite children to choose by pointing, naming, or holding a card. Let children pass; return to them gently later.
Ask two contrasting questions: ‘Did we all choose the same thing?’ and ‘What could we ask a friend about their choice?’
Close by showing the child page: ‘You will circle one choice and draw what it looks like for you.’
blocks.teacher_words: ‘My choice can be different from yours. We can listen to both.’
blocks.child_action: Point to or name a preference; listen while another child shares.
blocks.look_for: Can the child make a choice and attend to another child’s response?
blocks.assistant: Hold the cards where every child can see; offer a quieter pointing option for children who prefer it.
blocks.materials: One teacher set of five choice cards (Child materials p.1); child page preview (p.2).

blocks.title: Practice / Small Group + STEM
blocks.goal: Represent a preference on paper; count 1–5 concrete blocks one by one.
blocks.prepare: Print one My Choice page per child. Set crayons at each table. Put five blocks per participating child at the STEM station; have spare blocks available.
steps: Station A, 10:40–10:55: model circling one pictured choice or the ‘something else’ option. Children then draw themselves doing it. Scribe a child’s words without correcting the choice.
Station B, 10:55–11:10: each child builds with up to five blocks. Teacher models touching one block for each number word. Invite the child to count their own structure.
Ask: ‘What did you make?’ and ‘How many blocks did you use?’ Offer a recount when fingers move faster than number words.
Record one brief observation per child. Clear materials together by 11:15.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘Touch one block when you say one number. Let’s see what you made.’
blocks.child_action: Circle and draw; build, touch-count 1–5, and describe or point to the structure.
blocks.look_for: One-to-one correspondence up to five; child’s own choice is represented, not copied from a neighbor.
blocks.assistant: Lead or supervise the opposite station. If staffing is limited, run stations sequentially and reduce group size rather than leaving children without supervision.
blocks.materials: My Choice worksheet (p.2), one per child; crayons; five blocks per child at the active station; observation sheet in teacher guide.

blocks.title: Book Time · before nap
blocks.goal: Listen to a short original story and notice that a character tries again.
blocks.prepare: Print one display copy of the four story pages; review the pictures and short text before lunch.
steps: Show the cover of ‘Nia Tries Again.’ Say the title and let children notice the blocks.
Read each of the four pages slowly. Pause once after the tower falls: ‘What could Nia do next?’
At the end ask: ‘What did Nia and Eli like to do?’ Accept pointing to the pictures.
Put the story away and use the remaining part of the DOT window to settle for nap.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘Nia tried again. You can try again in your own way, too.’
blocks.child_action: Look, listen, predict or point, then prepare for rest.
blocks.look_for: Can the child point to or describe one event in the story?
blocks.assistant: Support the settling routine while the lead teacher reads; do not treat the whole 20-minute window as reading time.
blocks.materials: ‘Nia Tries Again,’ four printable story pages (Child materials pp.4–7), one teacher display set.

blocks.title: Review / Small Circle
blocks.goal: Recall an idea from the morning or the story and listen to a peer.
blocks.prepare: Keep two choice cards and the third story page (child PDF p.6) nearby.
steps: Invite children to look at the story illustration. Ask what Nia did after the tower fell.
Show two choice cards and ask: ‘Can two friends like different things?’ Invite one or two responses.
Invite a child to show an action they tried today. Allow a gesture instead of speech.
Transition directly to the self-portrait activity.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘I heard two different choices. Both belong in our classroom.’
blocks.child_action: Recall, point, speak, gesture, or listen.
blocks.look_for: Can the child revisit one idea without needing an exact verbal answer?
blocks.assistant: Invite quieter children with a card to point to; do not force a public turn.
blocks.materials: Two choice cards and the third story page (child PDF p.6), already printed for earlier blocks.

blocks.title: Book Time · after nap
blocks.goal: Reconnect with a familiar story after waking.
blocks.prepare: Have the same teacher story copy at the circle.
steps: Show the cover and one familiar picture; name the story briefly.
Re-read only the third story page (child PDF p.6), then ask: “What changed when Nia tried again?”
Move immediately into the Review / Small Circle questions.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘Let’s look again. What do you notice this time?’
blocks.child_action: Point to a picture or offer one observation.
blocks.look_for: Re-engages with a familiar book after nap.
blocks.assistant: Help late wakers join quietly; do not extend this slot if the wake-up routine runs long.
blocks.materials: Same teacher story copy; no extra printing. This four-minute placement is a prototype choice, not a separate DOT time slot.

blocks.title: Art / Craft
blocks.goal: Create a self-portrait that shows a chosen activity.
blocks.prepare: Print one portrait page per child. Put crayons, child-safe scissors, and glue sticks on the table. Pre-cut badges for children who need help.
steps: Point to the large drawing frame: ‘Draw yourself doing something you enjoy.’ Model a stick person on scrap paper without giving a finished picture to copy.
Children choose one printed activity badge at the bottom, cut or receive it pre-cut, and glue it to the frame. ‘Something else’ remains available.
Invite each child to tell the teacher about the drawing. Write their words on the line if they want.
Display or file the work and clear the table by 16:00.
blocks.teacher_words: ‘This is your picture. It can look different from mine or anyone else’s.’
blocks.child_action: Draw, select a badge, cut or receive help, glue, and share if desired.
blocks.look_for: Child represents an idea of their own and uses tools with appropriate help.
blocks.assistant: Support scissors and glue, help with cleanup, and keep one-to-one support available.
blocks.materials: One Self-Portrait page (p.3) per child; crayons, child-safe scissors, glue sticks; optional pre-cut badge strips.

observation_prompts: Choice: point / name / gesture / pass — what support helped?
Listening: notice a peer’s different choice — independent / prompted / not yet observed.
Counting: touch-count up to five — independent / prompted / not yet observed.
Story: recall or point to the ‘try again’ moment — independent / prompted / not yet observed.
